title: December, 2017
venue: Arthur's site · the coastal weeklies · from 2017 the aggregator
logline: Does Chloe come home. She's in the rental. Her parents' old house. Four days. She doesn't tell him. He sees the lockbox open.

panels.composition: Main street, December, rain. WOOD walking BARNABY II past the row of houses. Her parents' old house: the lockbox open, a light on, a car with Washington plates.

image.prompt: a thin man walking a three-legged dog past an old wooden house in December rain, the key lockbox on its door hanging open, a light inside, a car with Washington plates in the drive, clean ink with a gray wash
image.notes: Washington plates this time. Letter after.

panels.composition: Wood stopped. The pup sitting because Wood stopped. The window. A silhouette — hers. Pinned hair.

image.prompt: a man and a dog stopped on a rainy sidewalk looking at a lit house window with the silhouette of a woman with pinned-up hair, no words

panels.composition: Wood's hand, lifting, as if to knock on air. Lowering.

image.prompt: close-up of a man's hand rising as if to knock on nothing and then lowering, rain, no words

panels.composition: Walking on. The house behind. The silhouette in the window has turned toward the street. The strip doesn't say whether she saw him. Christmas Eve was 1999; this is the same walk, eighteen years on.

image.prompt: a thin man and a dog walking away down a rainy street from an old house where a woman's silhouette in the lit window has turned toward the street, no words
image.notes: Rhymes with dw_1999-12-24. Same house, same walk, a silhouette that might have seen him.

art.line: razor-sharp brush and ink; the pup's weight learned; Sundays wet-on-wet
art.palette: dailies: ink and one tone. Sundays: gray-green, fog, rust, bruised dusk

notes: She's four houses down, renting her own childhood house. He doesn't knock. She might have seen.
